title: Find a square with lambda
description: Use lambda to multiply a number by itself. Call it with a number and print the answer.
solution:
square = lambda n: n * n
print(square(7))

title: Sort names by length with lambda
description: Use this list of names: Christopher, Ayesha, and Ali. Use sorted() with lambda to put the shortest name first, then print the list.
solution:
names = ["Christopher", "Ayesha", "Ali"]
sorted_names = sorted(names, key=lambda name: len(name))
print(sorted_names)
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Use lambda inside sort(key=...) or sorted(key=...).
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: sorted() uses the lambda as its key. len(name) tells Python to sort names from shortest to longest.
commonMistakes: Pass a list of names and use key=lambda name: len(name). Do not sort unrelated number pairs.

validation.feedback: Use lambda inside sort(key=...) or sorted(key=...).

title: Keep even numbers with filter
description: Make a list of numbers. Use filter() and lambda to keep only even numbers. Print the result.
solution:
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
evens = list(filter(lambda n: n % 2 == 0, numbers))
print(evens)
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Use filter(lambda ..., values) and display the result.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: This task gives you practice with filter values with lambda. The reference solution is only one example; other working approaches are accepted when they use the required Python feature.
commonMistakes: Check brackets and quotes, use the correct indentation, and make sure you actually use the Python feature asked for in the task.

validation.feedback: Use filter(lambda ..., values) and display the result.

title: Double numbers with map
description: Use the numbers [2, 3, 4]. Use map() with lambda to double each number, then print the result.
solution:
numbers = [2, 3, 4]
doubled = list(map(lambda number: number * 2, numbers))
print(doubled)
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Use map(lambda ..., values) and display the result.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: map() applies the lambda to every item. The lambda multiplies each number by 2.
commonMistakes: Use * 2 to double each number. ** 2 makes a square instead.

validation.feedback: Use map() with lambda and multiply each number by 2.
